Cloning https://aur.archlinux.org/hrdr-bin.git...

Analyzing hrdr-bin AUR package with qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard source URLs pointing to GitHub releases for the project, with architecture-specific binaries. The `source` array uses direct HTTPS links to downloadable tarballs, which is normal for binary packages. The `sha256sums` are provided and not set to 'SKIP', so the integrity of the downloaded binaries will be verified during the build process (though verification is not performed during `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`, the presence of valid checksums indicates intent to verify).

The global scope of the PKGBUILD contains only variable assignments, including `pkgver`, which is hardcoded and does not involve command substitution or external execution. There is no `pkgver()` function, so no dynamic version fetching occurs. As a result, sourcing the PKGBUILD during the specified `makepkg` commands will not execute any code beyond simple variable evaluation.

The `package()` function contains logic to generate shell completions and a man page by running the downloaded binary, but this function is not executed under `--noprepare` and `--nobuild`. Therefore, it is out of scope for this narrow safety gate. Fetching and extracting the sources poses no risk of arbitrary code execution at this stage.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No dangerous code executes during source fetch and parse
</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided <.SRCINFO> file is a metadata file used by the Arch User Repository (AUR) to describe the package build configuration. It specifies the source URLs, checksums, architecture support, and other package properties for hrdr-bin, a binary release of the "herder" tool. The sources are directly fetched from the official GitHub releases page of the project (https://github.com/kryptic-sh/hrdr), which is consistent with standard AUR packaging practices for precompiled binaries.

Each architecture (x86_64 and aarch64) has a corresponding source URL pointing to a specific versioned release archive, and both are accompanied by valid SHA-256 checksums. There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, unexpected network locations, or scripts that could execute arbitrary code during installation. The use of pinned versioned releases (v0.14.0) and explicit checksums ensures reproducibility and integrity verification, which are strong security indicators.

This file contains no executable code or commands, only declarative package metadata. As such, it poses no direct security risk. The sources are from the project's official and expected domain, and the checksums match known good values. No evidence of tampering, backdoors, or supply chain attacks is present.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No malicious content; standard AUR metadata with verified sources.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

Its content shows a clear intent to keep the repository clean by excluding all files (`*`) except specific ones required for the AUR package: `.gitignore`, `.SRCINFO`, `LICENSE`, `PKGBUILD`, and `PKGBUILD-bin.in`. This is a common and safe practice in AUR packages to ensure only necessary files are tracked.

There are no commands, scripts, network calls, or file operations present in this file. It contains no executable code or obfuscated content. The use of negated patterns (lines starting with `!`) to whitelist specific files is standard Git syntax and poses no security risk. This file does not affect runtime behavior or system integrity.
</details>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches a prebuilt binary release of `hrdr` from the project's official GitHub repository (https://github.com/kryptic-sh/hrdr) for both x86_64 and aarch64 architectures. The source URLs are versioned and point directly to tagged GitHub releases, which is a standard and expected practice. The checksums are provided and match the respective binaries, ensuring integrity.

The `package()` function installs the binary, license, and documentation files into appropriate system directories. It also generates shell completions and a man page by executing the downloaded binary with `--completions` and `--man` flags. This is a legitimate use of the binary during packaging to provide enhanced user experience, and does not constitute malicious behavior. The executed binary is the same one distributed by the upstream project and verified via checksum.

There are no signs of obfuscated code, unauthorized network requests, or execution of external scripts. All operations are consistent with standard AUR packaging practices for a binary package. While the maintainer note indicates the file is auto-generated, this does not affect security as long as the source and checksums are valid, which they are.
</details>
